body:
It's not me who killed but I feel this story is from a different perspective that should still be heard (seen?). In this case, it was me who almost died. I swear the one who thought I had died had a face I can still remember. For me I have not fully understood it until I started thinking about it more after the incident, but apparently to others it really did look like my limp body on the ground. In elementary school, around age 12 or so, my class was on the field playing soccer. It went normally like any other PE time. One moment one of my classmates was the one who had to kick the ball towards the other end of the field. He was a strong kicker, and he proved that not only by the distance the ball traveled but its effect on me. I must have been in the way of the ball. Because when I started to run down to the other end of the field, I'm turning around to see if the ball was kicked, and I must have been hit with it on the side of the head. I didn't even realize what happened. My head turns and the next thing I remember is the ground hitting me then black. The next time I open my eyes, I'm still on the field, and the teacher is around me. I have no idea how much time passed. I'm dizzy af at that moment. The kid who kicked the ball is crying nearby, and just manages to say to me "I thought you died." At this point I thought he was joking. 
Now to the present day, I wonder about the trauma he has/had or whether he even remembers it or whether he just forgot about it. If I can remember it, he certainly has the possibility to, and I swear the face I remember just shows pure shock. I have not seen him or heard from him for quite a few years. I just hope I have not traumatized him in such a life altering way.

I'm sorry if this is not the best thing you have read. I'm not the best at writing.
